reasons: Enum values are not enforced by the database.

terms.meaning: a fixed list of allowed named values
deleting a parent also deletes its linked child rows
a link between two tables that lets code move between related rows

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and setup
sections.what: Brings in column types, the enum tools and the link to the shared base.
sections.why: Likely reason: the classes below need these tools.
sections.watch_out: The Enum column type is imported but not used for any column.

sections.name: AssetType
sections.title: Supported asset kinds
sections.what: Lists the asset kinds the app accepts: solar PV, wind and storage.
sections.why: Likely reason: one fixed place to check which asset types are valid.
sections.watch_out: Only solar PV has modeling code in this packet, so other types may not produce results.

sections.name: ProjectStatus
sections.title: Project lifecycle states
sections.what: Lists the three states a project can be in: active, archived and deleted.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the app hide or keep projects as they age.
sections.watch_out: Deletion is normally a status change, so deleted projects still exist in the database.

sections.name: Project
sections.title: Main project record
sections.what: Defines the project record with name, type, location, owner, timestamps, status, metadata and links to every related table.
sections.why: Likely reason: one central record that other data hangs from.
sections.watch_out: Deleting the row itself removes all linked child records through cascade settings.

summary: Defines the main project record and the lists of allowed asset types and status values.
purpose: Holds each benchmarking project and links it to its sources, comparables, inputs, models, schedules, exports and reasoning.
why: Likely reason: the project is the top-level container that everything else belongs to.
how: 1) The asset type list names the supported kinds. 2) The status list names active, archived and deleted. 3) The project record holds name, type, location, owner, timestamps, status and metadata. 4) Links connect related tables, so deleting a project removes its children.
inputs: Project name, type, location and metadata from the create route.
risks: The enum lists exist, but the columns store plain text, so the database accepts typos. Deleting a project row removes many child rows.
debug: If a project does not appear, check its status value and any filter used. If a project cannot be created, check that created_by points to an existing user.
